newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Asia Pacific 97, 98 growth seen around 7.4 pct-ADB.
newsitem.headline: Asia Pacific 97, 98 growth seen around 7.4 pct-ADB.

text.p: Economic growth in the Asia Pacific region slowed to 7.4 percent in 1996 from 8.2 percent the previous year, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) said in its annual report on Thursday.
Growth in the region "is expected to stabilise around this (7.4 percent) level for 1997 and 1998," the Manila-based institution said in its Asian Development Outlook.

But despite the slower growth in most Asian economies last year, the region recorded another year of healthy economic performance and continued to outperform other developing regions, the ADB said in the report.
The ADB cited a sharp drop in export growth, particularly in electronics, and the dollar's appreciation against the yen as some of the reasons for the decline in the region's growth.
It also said the loss by some countries such as Thailand, of their comparative advantage in labour-intensive product lines, had affected economic growth.
"To restore rapid growth, such countries may need fundamental changes such as shifting production to cheaper places and enhancing productivity," the report said.
